headline: PM Tarique Rahman reaches Tokyo on four-day official visit to boost ties
summary: The visit aims to deepen bilateral relations, attract Japanese investment, and expand trade and development cooperation between the two nations.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Narita International Airport this morning for a four-day official visit to Japan, following an invitation from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with PM Takaichi on October 27, which will be followed by a joint press announcement and a luncheon.
During the visit, the PM will meet with Japanese government officials, business leaders, and development institutions, and will deliver the keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum.
Key discussions will focus on the implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), expanding market access for Bangladeshi products, and strengthening business engagement.
The two nations will explore cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, and human resource development.
The itinerary includes visits to a Toyota factory in Nagoya, the UNIQLO headquarters, and an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, Chiba.

Up to eight Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) are under discussion, with three to four expected to be signed during the visit, covering sectors like civil aviation, trade, and environmental conservation.
The leaders are also expected to discuss regional stability, a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis, and cooperation in addressing the energy crisis.

Japan has remained a major development partner for Bangladesh since 1972, supporting critical infrastructure like the Dhaka Metro Rail and the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

headline: Air quality alert: Dhaka ranks 4th most polluted city worldwide
summary: The capital city faced severe air pollution levels on Monday morning, placing it among the top five most polluted cities globally.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the 4th most polluted city in the world as of Monday morning.
The ranking is based on real-time air quality index (AQI) data, highlighting the critical levels of pollutants in the city's air.
Severe air pollution in the capital often impacts public health, causing respiratory issues for millions of residents.
The city continues to struggle with high levels of particulate matter, a common occurrence during the winter months in the region.
